newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl won't rule out reshuffle before poll - TV.
newsitem.headline: Kohl won't rule out reshuffle before poll - TV.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl was quoted on Thursday as saying he saw no need for a cabinet reshuffle at the moment, but did not rule out the possiblity before September 1998 general elections.
"I have no reason to be dissatisfied with my cabinet colleagues," Kohl told ZDF television in the transcript of an interview released ahead of transmission.
"We're talking here about topical political matters and for me at this moment there is no cabinet reshuffle."

Asked whether "at this moment" meant he was ruling out a reshuffle for this year and next year, Kohl replied: "There I am still completely open. But I don't want to expound now on what I am going to do before the election."

Kohl said Post Minister Wolfgang Boetsch would leave his job at the end of the year as already agreed, which would change the balance of the parties in the ruling coalition. This would have to be discussed, the chancellor said.
"It is right that everyone says this is the domain of the chancellor. Because of that I don't intend to discuss this in public and I think the current discussion is totally unnecessary." he said.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Thursday repeated a call for a cabinet reshuffle soon, saying a shake-up would make Kohl's 17-member cabinet more effective in the run-up to next year's election.
